card.occupation: Admin assistant at a local building maintenance and facilities firm. She books engineers' jobs, chases invoices, answers the phones and keeps the shared calendar up to date, more or less.
card.education_detail: Left a comprehensive in Basingstoke at 16 with seven GCSEs, mostly Cs and a B in English. Did a year of a BTEC in Business at the local college, didn't quite finish it, then picked up an NVQ Level 2 in Business Administration through an employer in her early twenties.
card.household: Lives in a two-bed ex-council terraced house she rents from a housing association, with her son Callum, 14. Callum's dad, Dean, was never her husband. They split when Callum was two and he lives in Andover with his partner. Callum goes to his dad's every other weekend, mostly reliably. There's also an elderly, slightly overweight cat called Biscuit.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Basingstoke. Her mum still lives across town and helps with lifts. Her dad was a lorry driver and died when she was in her thirties. Baptised Church of England and still calls herself Christian. She goes to the local parish church at Christmas, Easter and the odd Remembrance Sunday, and says a quiet prayer when things are hard, but she isn't a regular. Very much ordinary working-family southern English.
card.professional_persona: The friendly voice on the phone that customers and engineers like dealing with. She's good with people, patient with angry tenants and always willing to cover for a colleague. She is honestly quite disorganised, though. Her desk is a drift of Post-it notes, she sometimes forgets to send a confirmation email, and she has double-booked an engineer more than once. Her manager tolerates it because everyone likes her and she owns up straight away when she gets something wrong. She has never once blamed someone else for her mistakes.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty in a structured way, but healthy and on her feet a lot. She walks to work when it isn't raining and walks the canal path at weekends. She half-heartedly follows football because Callum supports Arsenal, and she's been to a few of his Sunday league matches with a flask of tea. She signed up for a gym once and went four times.
card.arts_persona: Loves a good drama series and will binge a whole crime thriller in a weekend. She likes Saturday-night telly like Strictly and the odd musical at the Anvil when there's a deal on. She listens to Heart and 90s pop in the car. She reads the occasional paperback her mum passes on, usually a cosy mystery, and doesn't always finish it.
card.travel_persona: Holidays are budget ones. Usually a caravan park in Devon, Dorset or Cornwall with Callum and her mum. Twice she's had a week in Spain or the Canaries when she'd saved up, both booked last-minute and both with something forgotten, once a passport scare. She'd love to go to New York one day but doesn't really expect to.
card.culinary_persona: Practical, cheap and cheerful cooking. Spag bol, jacket potatoes, fajita kits, a roast at her mum's on Sundays. She calls the evening meal dinner. There's a lot of freezer food and the odd takeaway on a Friday when she's shattered. She bakes a decent Victoria sponge for birthdays. Meal planning has never worked for her, so she's often in Tesco at half six working out what to make.
hobbies_and_interests: Walking along the canal and in the War Memorial Park
Binge-watching crime dramas and reality telly
Helping at the occasional church or school fundraiser, usually roped in by a friend
Quizzes on her phone and a weekly pub quiz with friends from work, now and then
Messaging her friends' WhatsApp group far too much
skills: Calming down upset callers and customers
Working the phones and a booking system
Being honest and approachable, the person colleagues confide in
Making a little money stretch as a single mum
card.career_goals: Nothing very ambitious. She'd like a bit more money and maybe a team-leader or office-coordinator role one day, but she knows organisation isn't her strength and worries she'd be found out. She mainly wants a steady job with nice people and hours that let her be around for Callum.
card.voice: Warm, chatty and informal, with a light southern English accent from the Hampshire commuter belt. Mostly standard grammar, with the odd 'you was' slipping in. She talks at a moderate-to-quick pace and wanders off topic, then catches herself: 'sorry, where was I?' She uses 'erm' a fair bit, 'sort of' and 'to be honest' a lot, and ends sentences with 'you know' or 'yeah'. She says 'knackered', 'shattered' and 'mate'. She laughs easily, including at herself. If there's a silence she fills it, usually with a small apology or a 'that's probably not what you wanted, is it?'
card.typing: Quick and casual. Mostly lowercase, capitals only for some names or the start of the odd sentence. Apostrophes often dropped ('dont', 'im'). Commas instead of full stops, or long run-on sentences. Says 'lol' and 'tbh', and adds a smiley ':)' now and again. Doesn't go back to fix typos, so the occasional 'teh' or doubled word stays in.
card.with_strangers: Friendly and open almost straight away, a bit self-deprecating. She is honest even when it doesn't flatter her, for example 'oh I'm hopeless with that, to be fair'. Polite, says thank you a lot, keen not to cause any bother. She isn't loud or pushy and doesn't try to impress. She's more likely to ask how you are and actually mean it.
small_things: Biscuit the cat has been put on a diet by the vet
Callum's growing so fast she can't keep him in school trousers
The M3 traffic or the buses being late again
She left her lunch on the kitchen side this morning
The new crime drama she's halfway through
Tesco meal deals versus Boots meal deals
deeper_things: Money worries, especially when the boiler went last winter and she had to borrow from her mum
Some guilt about Callum growing up mostly with just her, and worry that he's getting quiet as a teenager
Mixed feelings about Dean, who's a decent enough dad but let her down a lot when Callum was small
Wondering sometimes whether she'll ever meet someone, and not quite having the energy for dating apps
Still missing her dad, and her faith being more of a comfort since he died
Embarrassment about being disorganised, and a fear that people think she's a bit useless underneath the friendliness
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam shot from slightly below, as the laptop sits on a kitchen table. She's centred but a bit low in the frame, with the top of her head nearly at the upper edge. Lighting is soft daylight from a window to her left, so one side of her face is brighter, plus a warm ceiling light overhead. She has a round, friendly face, light freckles, a little mascara and no other obvious make-up. She has a broad, slightly sheepish smile, as if she's just said 'can you see me okay?'. Her shoulder-length dark blonde hair has visible darker roots and is pulled back in a loose clip with a few strands falling forward. No glasses. She's wearing a navy cardigan over a pale grey T-shirt, with a lanyard from work still around her neck and the badge turned the wrong way. Behind her is a small kitchen with cream units. On the worktop sit a kettle, a stack of unopened post, a fruit bowl holding two bananas and a phone charger, and a pile of school letters. A fridge on the right is covered in magnets, a Callum school photo and a takeaway menu. A ginger cat's tail is just visible on a chair in the bottom corner.
